Visakhapatnam- 530 027 |campus = |website = [https://web.archive.org/web/20120330212508/http://drdo.gov.in/drdo/labs/NSTL/English/index.jsp?pg=homebody.jsp&labhits=3043] |footnotes = }} The '''Naval Science and Technological Laboratory''' ('''NSTL''') is an Indian defence laboratory of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO), located in [[Visakhapatnam]]. Its main function is the research and development of underwater weapons and associated systems. NSTL is organized under DRDO's Directorate of Naval R&D. The present director of NSTL is Dr. Abraham Varughese and Director General (DG) is Dr Y. Sreenivas Rao, Distinguished Scientist .{{cite web | url=https://www.drdo.gov.in/labs-establishment/director/naval-science-technological-laboratory-nstl | title=Director | Defence Research and Development Organisation - DRDO, Ministry of Defence, Government of India }} == History == NSTL was established on 20 August 1969 to undertake research and development of major naval systems and underwater weapons for the [[Indian Navy]] to make it self-reliant.{{usurped|1=[https://archive.today/20010306222156/http://www.drdo.org/labs/nr&d/nstl/history.shtml NSTL History]}} == Areas of work == NSTL is involved in the design, development, testing, evaluation and productionization of underwater weapons and their associated weapon control systems. These include [[torpedo]]es, mines, decoys, targets, simulators, Fire Control Systems and weapon launchers. The lab is also involved in investigating [[hydrodynamic]] parameters and structural design of surface and submerged naval platforms and in evolving design criteria through model studies and simulation. NSTL is also involved in developing Warship Technologies, [[Stealth Technology]] for ships and Hydro-dynamic research services. NSTL also develops specialized materials for Marine Applications, including materials for mitigation of [[Radar]], [[Infrared|IR]], Magnetic, Acoustic and [[ELFE]] Signatures leading to stealthier platforms. === Facilities === NSTL is equipped with laboratories and Hydrodynamic research facilities including a High Speed Towing Tank (HSTT), a Cavitation Tunnel and a Wind Tunnel. They also have Acoustic, Shock, Noise and Vibration Test Facilities that are used to measure, study and analyze the mitigation of underwater noise generated by ships and submarines. {{cite web |title=Facilities of NSTL |url=http://drdo.gov.in/drdo/labs/NSTL/English/index.jsp?pg=facility.jsp |website=DRDO |access-date=13 July 2024 |archive-date=30 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120330213159/http://drdo.gov.in/drdo/labs/NSTL/English/index.jsp?pg=facility.jsp |url-status=bot: unknown }} == Projects and Products == * [[Maareech ATDS]] * [[Autonomous underwater vehicle|Autonomous underwater vehicles]] ** [[#High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (HEAUV)|High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle]] ** [[#Man-Portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (MP-AUVs)|Man-portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (MP-AUVs)]] * Torpedoes ** [[Torpedo Advanced Light Shyena]] ** [[Torpedo Advanced Light Shyena#Advanced Light-Weight Torpedo (ALWT)|Advanced Light Weight Torpedo]] ** [[Varunastra (torpedo)|Varunastra HWT]] ** [[Varunastra (torpedo)#Thermal Heavy Weight Torpedo Shakti|Shakti Thermal Torpedo]] ** [[Varunastra (torpedo)#Electronic Heavy Weight Torpedo Takshak|Takshak Torpedo]] * [[Naval Science and Technological Laboratory#Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM)|Multi-Influence Ground Mine]] (MIGM) * [[Naval Science and Technological Laboratory#Air Droppable Container (ADC-150)|Air Droppable Container (ADC-150)]] == High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (HEAUV) == DRDO's NSTL in partnership with the [[Cochin Shipyard]] is developing the HEAUV [[autonomous underwater vehicle]]. The HEAUV, first reported in 2024, is undergoing multiple trials. The vehicle has a weight of {{Convert|6|short ton|kg|abbr=on}}, length of around {{Convert|10|m||abbr=on}} and diameter of {{Convert|1|m||abbr=on}}. As for the performance, it has a maximum depth of {{Convert|300|m||abbr=on}}, endurance of 15 days at an economical speed of {{Convert|3|kn|km/h|abbr=on}} and a maximum speed of {{Convert|8|kn|km/h|abbr=on}}. It can be mounted with swappable mission-specific payloads. The equipment include:–{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-03-12 |title=High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (HEAUV) |url=https://alphadefense.in/index.php/2024/03/12/high-endurance-autonomous-underwater-vehicle-heauv/ |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=alphadefense.in |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2025-04-20 |title=India's High Endurance AUV Program Undergoes Developmental Trials |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2025/04/indias-high-endurance-auv-program-undergoes-developmental-trials/ |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}} * [[X band]] 360° surveillance radar for [[Intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance|Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance]] (ISR) operations, developed by [[LRDE]]. * {{Convert|45|bar||abbr=on}}-rated mast mounted [[radome]] to house [[Collision avoidance system|collision avoidance radar]]. * Communication systems (including acoustic, [[UHF]], [[C band (IEEE)|C band]], [[Communications satellite|SATCOM]]). * Front and flank array [[sonars]] as primary underwater sensors, [[Side-scan sonar|side-scan sonars]] for [[mine countermeasure]] (MCM) operations developed by [[NPOL]]. * Array of batteries for [[propulsion system]] which includes electric motors connected to [[composite propeller]]s. * Capsule-based [[hydrogen fuel cell]] power plant (under development by [[NMRL]]. In the first week of March 2024, the maiden surface trials of the HEAUV was conducted by DRDO and CSL at the [[Cochin Shipyard|International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF)]] Jetty in Kochi. All the system parameters were met during the trials.{{Cite web |last=Admin |date=2024-04-09 |title=DRDO's AUV Conducts Successful Surface Run |url=https://raksha-anirveda.com/drdos-auv-conducts-successful-surface-run/ |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=raksha-anirveda.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite tweet |number=1765715469946826808 |user=DRDO_India |title=Maiden Surface run of High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (HEAUV) meeting all the mission parameters were carried out successfully at Cochin Shipyard, International Ship Repair Facility(ISRF) Jetty, Kochi. |date=2024-03-07 |access-date=2025-04-22}}{{Cite tweet |number=1765917170427670683 |user=cslcochin |title=Proud moment for India, DRDO, and Cochin Shipyard Limited! 🇮🇳 The nation's first fully indigenous High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle integrated at CSL has completed its maiden trials at CSL's ISRF facility... |date=2024-03-07 |access-date=2025-04-22}} In late March 2025, DRDO conducted Lake Trials of the HEAUV during which vehicle dynamics, in both submerged and surfaced conditions, was tested successfully along with its Sonar and Communications suite.{{Cite tweet |number=1906400247452176655 |user=DRDO_India |title=High Endurance Autonomous Underwater Vehicle currently under development by NSTL has been successfully tested in lake. During the trials vehicle dynamics was proven in both surface and submerged condition through multiple runs with perfect performance of Sonars and Communication |date=2025-03-30 |access-date=2025-04-22}} In 2018, the [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]] had released a [[Request for Information]] (RFI) for the acquisition of eight HEAUVs for [[Indian Navy]]'s [[Anti-submarine warfare|ASW]], ISR and MCM operations as well as [[Bathymetry|bathymetric]] and [[Oceanography|oceanographic]] data gathering. Further, an [[Expression of Interest]] (EoI) was released to invite Indian companies to develop an HEAUV for just ASW operations. As of now, [[GRSE]] is also developing HEAUV-ASW expected to completed by 2027 along with its [[Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers#Neerakshi AUV|Neerakshi AUV]]. [[Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders]] also released an EoI for HEAUV-ASW development in 2023. == Man-Portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (MP-AUVs) == NSTL has developed a generation of Man-Portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (MP-AUVs) for [[mine countermeasure]] operations equipped with [[Side-scan sonar|side-scan sonars]] and underwater cameras. They will be tasked to detect and classify mine-like objects with assistance from deep learning based [[target recognition]]. Additionally, the AUVs employ [[underwater acoustic communication]] for inter-AUV data exchange. The field trials was completed at NSTL Harbour in November 2025.{{Cite press release |title=DRDO develops new generation Man-portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles for mine countermeasure missions |date=2025-11-14 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190096 |access-date=2025-11-15}}{{Cite web |last=Negi |first=Shivani SharmaManjeet |date=2025-11-15 |title=India develops next-gen autonomous underwater vehicles for mine warfare |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/india-develops-next-gen-autonomous-underwater-vehicles-for-mine-warfare-2820189-2025-11-15 |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Mayank |date=2025-11-14 |title=IAF Sukhoi-30 MKI to get advanced jammer pods; DRDO develops new autonomous underwater vehicles |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2025/Nov/14/iaf-sukhoi-30-mki-to-get-advanced-jammer-pods-drdo-develops-new-autonomous-underwater-vehicles |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} == Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM) == Multi-Influence Ground Mine (MIGM) is a tactical [[naval mine]] developed for the Indian Navy by NSTL in collaboration with [[HEMRL]] and [[TBRL]] as well as [[Bharat Dynamics Limited]] and Apollo Microsystems Limited as the production agency. The system is designed to counter stealth surface ships and submarines by detecting their various influences such as [[Acoustic signature|acoustic]], [[Magnetic field|magnetic]] and pressure signatures. On 5 May 2025, DRDO successfully undertook the combat firing (with reduced explosive) of the mine.{{Cite news |date=2025-05-05 |title=DRDO & Indian Navy conduct combat firing (with reduced explosive) of indigenous Multi-Influence Ground Mine |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2127155 |access-date=2025-05-06 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}{{Cite news |date=2025-05-05 |title=DRDO, Navy conduct successful trial of MIGM |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/drdo-navy-conduct-successful-trial-of-migm/articleshow/120904004.cms |access-date=2025-05-06 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite web |title=Multi - Influential Ground Mines (MIGM) {{!}} Official Website of Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India |url=https://bdl-india.in/migm |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=bdl-india.in}} The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) of [[Ministry of Defence (India)|India's Defence Ministry]] cleared multiple procurement projects including that of MIGM for the Indian Navy on 3 July 2026.{{Cite press release |title=DAC approves capital acquisition proposals worth Rs 52,000 crore to enhance combat readiness of Defence Forces |date=2026-07-03 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2280728®=3&lang=1 |access-date=2026-07-02}}{{Cite web |date=2026-07-03 |title=Defence acquisition proposals worth Rs 52,000 cr cleared, will boost combat readiness of forces |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/defence-acquisition-council-rs-52000-crore-procurement-akash-tarang-mrsam-10770024/ |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} == Air Droppable Container (ADC-150) == The NSTL has developed the Air Droppable Container (ADC) 150 to enhance naval logistics. The container has a capacity of {{Convert|150|kg|lb|abbr=on}} and is meant to supply critical stores/equipment, medical assistance and others to [[Distress signal|distressed]] ships at blue sea, day from the coasts. While the NSTL was the nodal agency for the development programme, the [[Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment]] (ADRDE) developed the parachute system, the [[Defence Research and Development Laboratory]] (DRDL) provided instrument support for trials and the [[Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification]] (CEMILAC) was involved for the flight clearance & certification.{{Cite press release |title=DRDO & Indian Navy conduct in-flight release trials of indigenous Air Droppable Container ‘ADC-150’ from P8I Aircraft |date=2026-03-10 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2237814®=3&lang=1 |access-date=2026-03-11}} The ADC-150 was developed in a short timeframe to meet the [[Indian Navy]] requirements. The system has been tested four times between 21 February and 1 March 2026 by the Navy and DRDO through a range of extreme conditions. The flight trials were carried out off the coast of [[Goa]] from a [[P-8I Neptune]] aircraft. The system is expected to be inducted soon after the tests were conducted successfully. == See also == * [[DRDO]] == References == {{Reflist}}https://www.drdo.gov.in/labs-establishment/director/naval-science-technological-laboratory-nstl == External links == {{commons category|Naval Science and Technological Laboratory}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20120330212508/http://drdo.gov.in/drdo/labs/NSTL/English/index.jsp?pg=homebody.jsp&labhits=3043] {{DRDO Laboratories}} {{Authority control}} {{coord missing|Andhra Pradesh}} [[Category:Defence Research and Development Organisation laboratories]] [[Category:Research institutes in Andhra Pradesh]] [[Category:Research and development in India]] [[Category:Education in Visakhapatnam]] [[Category:1969 establishments in Andhra Pradesh]] [[Category:Research institutes established in 1969]]
